1#main: Whether it is permitted to spread kilayim beneath oneself, and the law of a pack-saddle and shrouds. In it are 15 seifim. It is permitted by Torah to sit on bedding of kilayim, as it says, "it shall not ascend upon you"—but you may spread it beneath you. {Rama: And likewise it is permitted to raise them upon oneself not in the manner of warming, such as to spread a tent of kilayim over oneself (Tur); and likewise to spread a garment of kilayim over a vat in which one bathes in order to retain the heat (Mordechai, first chapter of Beitzah, and Hagahos Ashiri there)—for it is forbidden only in the manner of wearing or raising them upon oneself in the manner of warming.} And by rabbinic enactment, even ten mattresses one atop the other, and the lower one among them is kilayim—it is forbidden to sit on the upper one, lest a thread wrap upon his flesh. In what case is this said? With soft items such as sheets and garments; but pillows and cushions that are hard, and there is no concern lest a thread wrap upon him—it is permitted to sleep on them, provided his flesh does not touch them. In what case is this said? When they are empty and placed on a wooden or stone bench; but if they are full, or even if empty when they are placed on a bed or on straw—it is forbidden, because it bends beneath him and wraps upon his flesh. {Rama: And some say all this applies to kilayim d'oraisa; but with kilayim d'rabbanan that are hard, it is permitted to sit on them in every case, since when they are hard it is only d'rabbanan—they did not decree on hard items (Rashba siman 962). Nevertheless, l'chatchila one should not make items of kilayim (Kol Bo).}
2#main: These felt caps of ours—if they are sewn with linen, one must be careful not to raise them upon oneself and even not to spread them beneath him until they are sewn with silk or cotton. {Rama: All hard garments are permitted for spreading beneath him and forbidden to wear; and hard felt is permitted even for wearing, since even when soft they are only d'rabbanan (Tur). And some are stringent regarding wearing felt (Beit Yosef in the name of the Rambam).}
3#main: A large garment that has kilayim on one side—it is forbidden to wear it even from its other side, even though the side containing the kilayim is dragged along the ground.
4#main: It is forbidden to wear kilayim even casually, such as a child's tallit—even though an adult does not go out in it casually.
5#main: A person should not wear kilayim casually, even atop ten garments from which he derives no benefit at all—even to steal from the tax collector.
6#main: Tailors of garments sew in their usual manner, provided they do not intend for warmth because of the heat or because of rain; and the modest sew on the ground. And likewise sellers of garments sell in their usual manner, provided they do not intend for warmth because of the heat or because of rain; and the modest hang on a rod. {Rama: And some permit even wearing kilayim whenever he does not intend for his benefit, such as one who wears kilayim to pass the tax through it, or who wears them to show their measure if he wishes to sell them and the like (Tur, Rosh, and Semag).}
7#main: Shrouds for the dead are permitted to make from kilayim, even to bury him in them.
8#main: A donkey's pack-saddle—it is permitted to make it from kilayim and to sit on it, provided his flesh does not touch it; and he should not place this pack-saddle on his shoulder even to carry manure on it. And specifically when the kilayim is recognizable and known in the garment; but a garment in which kilayim was lost and its place is not recognizable—it is forbidden to make from it a pack-saddle for a donkey, since its place is not recognizable—lest he forget and take from it a patch to sew atop his garment; and he should not sell it to a gentile, lest the gentile resell it to an Israelite.
9#main: Towels with which one wipes the hands, and towels with which one dries utensils and floors, and with which one dries after washing, and towels for books—are forbidden because of kilayim, since the hands touch them and they wrap upon the hand constantly and become warmed. {Rama: And likewise it is forbidden to make towels that are spread on the table at which one eats (Rosh, general rule 6, and Chiddushei Agudah end of Beitzah), or that one reads upon in the synagogue from kilayim (Hagahos Ashiri, chapter Bnei HaIr), because sometimes one wipes his hands with them and becomes warmed in them.}
10#main: Towels with which one has a haircut—if one has a head-covering and wears it in the manner of wearing, it is forbidden because of kilayim.
11#main: A curtain—if it is soft, it is forbidden to make it from kilayim because the sun warms in it sometimes; and if it was hard, it is permitted. {Rama: But a curtain before the Holy Ark, or the cloths spread in the ark, or around the Torah—it is permitted for them to be of kilayim (there in Hagahos Ashiri).}
12#main: A person should not take a warm egg in a garment of kilayim in his hand, since once he is saved from being scalded by the egg's heat, it is considered benefit like preventing cold.
13#main: Ardilirin (meaning: a vessel worn under the shoe; and some make them of wool against the heel)—they contain no kilayim, for they are hard. (From Rashi's explanation in the name of the Geonic responsum.) They contain no kilayim. {Rama: A shoe that is kilayim and has no heel—it is permitted to wear it, for the skin of the foot is hard and one does not enjoy it like other skin of the body (Tur).}
14#main: There is no prohibition of kilayim except in garments that are worn in the manner of warming, such as a shirt, turban, pants, belt, cloak, and garments with which one covers the legs and the hands and the like; but small bells that people make on their wrists to tie money or spices in them, and a rag on which one places a poultice or a compress or a plaster and the like—these are permitted even though his flesh touches them, for there is no manner of warming in this. A leather or silk frontlet on which wool and linen threads hang loose upon a person's face in order to drive away flies—there is no kilayim in it, for there is no manner of warming in this.
15#main: Marks that launderers and fullers make on garments so that each recognizes his own—if the mark was of wool on linen or linen on wool, behold this is forbidden even though it is not important to him.
